'Put out' একটি phrasal verb যার অর্থ নিভিয়ে দেওয়া, তাই সঠিক বাক্য 'Put out the light'।

questions.question: Don't forget ---- your homework.
questions.explanation:
After 'forget', the to-infinitive is used, so 'to do' is correct.
'Forget'-এর পরে to-infinitive বসে, তাই 'to do' সঠিক।

questions.question: Rajshahi is ---- sugar growing areas in Bangladesh.
questions.explanation:
'One of the' is followed by a superlative and a plural noun, so 'one of the largest' is correct.
'One of the'-এর পরে superlative ও plural noun বসে, তাই 'one of the largest' সঠিক।

questions.question: Climate is a ---- of the environment.
questions.explanation:
Climate is best described as a 'state' of the environment.
জলবায়ুকে পরিবেশের একটি 'state' বা অবস্থা হিসেবে বর্ণনা করা হয়।

questions.question: How many types of infinitive are there?
questions.explanation:
The infinitive is of two kinds: the to-infinitive and the bare (zero) infinitive.
Infinitive দুই প্রকার: to-infinitive এবং bare বা zero infinitive।

questions.question: The passive form of the sentence 'Do away with it' will be ----
options: Let it be done away with
Let it has done away with it
Let it is to be done away with
Let it has to do away with
questions.explanation:
The passive of the imperative 'Do away with it' is 'Let it be done away with'.
'Do away with it' একটি imperative বাক্য, যার passive রূপ হলো 'Let it be done away with'।

questions.question: We waited until the plane ----.
questions.explanation:
'Until' already carries a negative sense, so a simple past ('took off') is used, not a negative verb.
'Until' শব্দটির মধ্যেই নেতিবাচক ভাব থাকে, তাই নেতিবাচক নয় বরং সাধারণ past ('took off') ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.question: 'Kazi has slept only two hours.' Here 'only' is ----
questions.explanation:
Here 'only' limits the phrase 'two hours' and functions as an adverb.
এখানে 'only' শব্দটি 'two hours'-কে সীমিত করছে এবং adverb হিসেবে কাজ করছে।

questions.question: The feminine form of the word 'Author' is:
questions.explanation:
The feminine form of 'Author' is 'Authoress'.
'Author' শব্দের স্ত্রীবাচক রূপ হলো 'Authoress'।

questions.question: The passive form of the sentence 'The pill tastes bitter' is ----
options: The pill was bitter when it was tasted
The pill was bitter when it tasted
The pill is bitter when it tastes
The pill is bitter when it is tasted
questions.explanation:
The passive form of 'The pill tastes bitter' is 'The pill is bitter when it is tasted'.
'The pill tastes bitter' বাক্যের passive রূপ হলো 'The pill is bitter when it is tasted'।

questions.question: 'The Patriot' is a poem written by ----
questions.explanation:
The poem 'The Patriot' was written by Robert Browning.
'The Patriot' কবিতাটি রবার্ট ব্রাউনিং রচনা করেন।

questions.question: I would be most obliged if you ---- pay later.
questions.explanation:
'Let' takes an object followed by a bare infinitive, so 'let me pay later' is correct.
'Let'-এর পরে object ও bare infinitive বসে, তাই 'let me pay later' সঠিক।

questions.question: The past participle form of the verb 'Fell' is ----
questions.explanation:
The verb 'fell' (to cut down a tree) is fell–felled–felled, so its past participle is 'felled'.
'Fell' (গাছ কাটা) ক্রিয়ার রূপ fell–felled–felled, তাই এর past participle হলো 'felled'।

questions.question: The ---- part of this book is interesting.
questions.explanation:
'Latter' means the second or later part of two things, so 'the latter part' is correct.
'Latter' অর্থ দুইয়ের মধ্যে শেষোক্ত বা পরবর্তী অংশ, তাই 'the latter part' সঠিক।

questions.question: Some of the boys ---- did not come.
questions.explanation:
The relative pronoun is omitted, so 'the boys I invited' (whom I invited) is correct.
এখানে relative pronoun উহ্য থাকে, তাই 'the boys I invited' (whom I invited) সঠিক।

questions.question: Tiger : Zoology :: Mars : ?
questions.explanation:
As the tiger is studied in Zoology, Mars (a planet) is studied in Astronomy.
যেমন বাঘ Zoology-তে অধ্যয়ন করা হয়, তেমনি মঙ্গল গ্রহ Astronomy-তে অধ্যয়ন করা হয়।

questions.question: Who is the playwright of the absurd drama "Waiting for Godot"?
questions.explanation:
The absurd play 'Waiting for Godot' was written by Samuel Beckett.
'Waiting for Godot' নামের অ্যাবসার্ড নাটকটি স্যামুয়েল বেকেট রচনা করেন।

questions.question: Indirect narration of: He said to me, "How happy you are!"
options: He told me that I was very happy
He told me I were happy
He told me that he was happy
He told me how I was happy
questions.explanation:
In indirect speech the exclamatory sentence becomes assertive: 'He told me that I was very happy'.
Indirect speech-এ exclamatory বাক্যটি assertive হয়ে যায়: 'He told me that I was very happy'।

questions.question: There are 10 ---- in a hundred.
questions.explanation:
The plural of the number 'ten' is 'tens', so there are 10 tens in a hundred.
'Ten' সংখ্যাটির plural হলো 'tens', তাই একশোতে ১০টি tens থাকে।

questions.question: In the sentence 'Wisdom is better than strength', the word 'strength' is a/an:
questions.explanation:
'Strength' denotes a quality that cannot be touched, so it is an abstract noun.
'Strength' এমন একটি গুণ বোঝায় যা স্পর্শ করা যায় না, তাই এটি abstract noun।

questions.question: Which sentence correctly asks what Dhaka is famous for?
questions.explanation:
The correct interrogative form is 'What is Dhaka famous for?', with the auxiliary placed before the subject.
সঠিক প্রশ্নবোধক রূপটি হলো 'What is Dhaka famous for?', যেখানে auxiliary verb subject-এর আগে বসে।

questions.question: What is the compound structure of "Though he is poor, he is honest"?
options: As he is poor, he is honest
Since he is poor, he is honest
questions.explanation:
A complex sentence with 'though' becomes compound using 'but': 'He is poor but honest'.
'Though'-যুক্ত complex বাক্যটি 'but' দিয়ে compound হয়: 'He is poor but honest'।

questions.question: Which one is the correct narration of: He told, 'Do the work'?
options: He said that do the work
He asked to do the work
questions.explanation:
The imperative 'Do the work' becomes 'He asked to do the work' in indirect speech.
Imperative বাক্য 'Do the work' indirect speech-এ হয় 'He asked to do the work'।

questions.question: Bangladesh was ---- in 1971.
questions.explanation:
The passive/past sense needs the past participle 'liberated': 'Bangladesh was liberated in 1971'.
এখানে past participle 'liberated' প্রয়োজন: 'Bangladesh was liberated in 1971'।

questions.question: 'We made her recite a poem' — the passive form is:
options: She was made to recite a poem.
She was made recited a poem.
A poem was made to be recited.
A poem was made recite by her.
questions.explanation:
In the passive of 'make + object + bare infinitive', a to-infinitive is used: 'She was made to recite a poem'.
'Make + object + bare infinitive'-এর passive-এ to-infinitive বসে: 'She was made to recite a poem'।

questions.question: Who is the modern philosopher who was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature?
questions.explanation:
The philosopher Bertrand Russell won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1950.
দার্শনিক বার্ট্রান্ড রাসেল ১৯৫০ সালে সাহিত্যে নোবেল পুরস্কার লাভ করেন।

questions.question: She succeeded ---- her good work.
questions.explanation:
'Because of' (a prepositional phrase) is followed by a noun phrase, so 'because of her good work' is correct.
'Because of'-এর পরে noun phrase বসে, তাই 'because of her good work' সঠিক।

questions.question: The incident took place long ago. Here the word 'ago' is a/an ----
questions.explanation:
Here 'ago' modifies the verb phrase and functions as an adverb.
এখানে 'ago' ক্রিয়াকে নির্দেশ করছে এবং adverb হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়েছে।

questions.question: I saw him play. — the passive form is:
options: He was seen by me play
Play was seen him by me
He was seen playing by me
He was seen to play by me
questions.explanation:
In the passive of 'see + object + bare infinitive', a to-infinitive is used: 'He was seen to play by me'.
'See + object + bare infinitive'-এর passive-এ to-infinitive বসে: 'He was seen to play by me'।

questions.question: The ministers arrived ---- a decision last night.
questions.explanation:
The correct collocation is 'arrive at a decision'.
সঠিক ব্যবহার হলো 'arrive at a decision'।

questions.question: Which one is used both as an auxiliary and a principal verb?
questions.explanation:
'Am' (a form of 'be') can work both as an auxiliary and as a principal verb.
'Am' (be-এর রূপ) auxiliary এবং principal verb উভয় হিসেবেই কাজ করতে পারে।

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct sentence?
options: A free press is the integral part of democracy.
A free press is integral to democracy.
A free press is an essentially integral to democracy.
A free press is the integral part to democracy.
questions.explanation:
The correct sentence is 'A free press is integral to democracy'.
সঠিক বাক্যটি হলো 'A free press is integral to democracy'।

questions.question: What is the plural form of 'Mr.'?
questions.explanation:
The plural form of 'Mr.' is 'Messrs'.
'Mr.'-এর plural রূপ হলো 'Messrs'।

questions.question: Anwar said, 'Let him say whatever he likes.' What is its indirect speech?
options: Anwar said that he may say whatever he liked
Anwar said that he might say whatever he liked
Anwar told that he might say whatever he likes
Anwar said he might say whatever he likes
questions.explanation:
In indirect speech the sentence becomes 'Anwar said that he might say whatever he liked'.
Indirect speech-এ বাক্যটি হয় 'Anwar said that he might say whatever he liked'।

questions.question: Select the best expression of the given sentence: "We were no more surprised than Rahman."
options: We were less surprised than Rahman
Rahman was less surprised than us.
We were as surprised as Rahman.
questions.explanation:
'No more...than' here means both were equally surprised: 'We were as surprised as Rahman'.
'No more...than' এখানে বোঝায় দুজনেই সমানভাবে বিস্মিত ছিল: 'We were as surprised as Rahman'।

questions.question: He is pro-European, because he ---- Europe.
questions.explanation:
'Pro-European' means favourable to Europe, i.e., he supports Europe.
'Pro-European' অর্থ ইউরোপের পক্ষে, অর্থাৎ সে ইউরোপকে সমর্থন করে।

questions.question: If a substance is cohesive, it tends to ----.
questions.explanation:
A cohesive substance tends to stick together.
Cohesive পদার্থ পরস্পর লেগে থাকার প্রবণতা রাখে।

questions.question: Select the correct sentence.
options: You may buy a pen at Taka 5
You may buy a pen by Taka 5
You may buy a pen for Taka 5
You may buy a pen with Taka 5
questions.explanation:
Price is expressed with 'for', so 'buy a pen for Taka 5' is correct.
মূল্য বোঝাতে 'for' ব্যবহৃত হয়, তাই 'buy a pen for Taka 5' সঠিক।

questions.question: What is the noun of the word 'Waste'?
questions.explanation:
The noun form of the word 'Waste' is 'Wastage'.
'Waste' শব্দের noun রূপ হলো 'Wastage'।

questions.question: The scissors ---- blunt.
questions.explanation:
'Scissors' is treated as a plural noun, so it takes 'are'.
'Scissors' plural noun হিসেবে গণ্য হয়, তাই এর সঙ্গে 'are' বসে।

questions.question: Which one of the following is a complex sentence?
options: Money is better servant than master
While he was walking in the garden a snake bit him.
questions.explanation:
'While he was walking in the garden a snake bit him' contains a subordinate clause, so it is a complex sentence.
'While he was walking in the garden a snake bit him' বাক্যে একটি অধীন clause আছে, তাই এটি complex sentence।

questions.question: Man hardly believes a liar, ----?
questions.explanation:
'Hardly' makes the sentence negative, so the question tag is positive: 'does he?'
'Hardly' বাক্যটিকে নেতিবাচক করে, তাই প্রশ্নবোধক tag হবে হ্যাঁ-বাচক: 'does he?'।

questions.question: Write down the minutes of the meeting. Here the word 'minutes' means:
questions.explanation:
The 'minutes' of a meeting means the written records of what was discussed.
সভার 'minutes' বলতে আলোচনার লিখিত বিবরণ বা কার্যবিবরণী বোঝায়।

questions.question: None of the students ---- a car.
questions.explanation:
'None of the' with a plural noun can take a plural verb, so 'have' is used here.
'None of the'-এর সঙ্গে plural noun থাকলে plural verb বসতে পারে, তাই এখানে 'have' ব্যবহৃত হয়েছে।

questions.question: 'Faerie Queene' is a ----
questions.explanation:
Edmund Spenser's 'The Faerie Queene' is an epic poem.
এডমন্ড স্পেন্সারের 'The Faerie Queene' একটি মহাকাব্য (epic)।

questions.question: 'Call me if you have any problems regarding your work.' Here 'regarding' is a/an ----
questions.explanation:
Here 'regarding' is followed by a noun and works as a preposition meaning 'about'.
এখানে 'regarding' একটি noun-এর আগে বসে preposition হিসেবে কাজ করছে, যার অর্থ 'সম্পর্কে'।

questions.question: The word 'Officialese' means ----
questions.explanation:
'Officialese' means the formal language typically used in offices and official documents.
'Officialese' অর্থ অফিস ও সরকারি নথিপত্রে ব্যবহৃত আনুষ্ঠানিক ভাষা।

questions.question: The teacher suggested that the students ---- honest in their responses.
questions.explanation:
After 'suggested that', the base form (subjunctive) is used, so 'be' is correct.
'Suggested that'-এর পরে base form (subjunctive) বসে, তাই 'be' সঠিক।

questions.question: In which sentence is 'like' used as a preposition?
options: He laughs like his father does.
He climbed the tree like a cat.
Like minded people are necessary to start a business.
questions.explanation:
In 'He climbed the tree like a cat', 'like' is followed by a noun and acts as a preposition.
'He climbed the tree like a cat' বাক্যে 'like'-এর পরে noun আছে, তাই এটি preposition।

questions.question: He deals ---- rice.
questions.explanation:
'Deal in' means to trade in something, so 'He deals in rice' is correct.
'Deal in' অর্থ কোনো কিছুর ব্যবসা করা, তাই 'He deals in rice' সঠিক।

questions.question: I have left the room but he ---- (enter) the room.
questions.explanation:
The present perfect 'has entered' suits the just-completed action, so 'he has entered the room'.
সদ্য সম্পন্ন কাজ বোঝাতে present perfect 'has entered' মানানসই, তাই 'he has entered the room'।

questions.question: Dhaka is becoming one of the ---- cities in Asia.
questions.explanation:
'One of the' is followed by a superlative, so 'busiest' is correct.
'One of the'-এর পরে superlative degree বসে, তাই 'busiest' সঠিক।

questions.question: A formal composition or speech expressing high praise of somebody is called ----
questions.explanation:
A 'eulogy' is a formal speech or writing that expresses high praise of someone.
'Eulogy' হলো কারও উচ্চ প্রশংসাসূচক আনুষ্ঠানিক বক্তৃতা বা রচনা।

questions.question: One's finger prints are ----.
options: different from those of any other person
questions.explanation:
For a correct comparison, we say 'different from those of any other person'.
সঠিক তুলনার জন্য বলা হয় 'different from those of any other person'।

questions.question: Would like ---- information, please.
questions.explanation:
'Information' is uncountable, so the quantifier 'some' is used.
'Information' uncountable noun, তাই এর সঙ্গে 'some' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'Jane Eyre'?
questions.explanation:
The novel 'Jane Eyre' was written by Charlotte Bronte.
'Jane Eyre' উপন্যাসটি শার্লট ব্রন্টি রচনা করেন।

questions.question: ---- to the market?
questions.explanation:
The correct form is 'With whom did you go to the market?', with the auxiliary before the subject.
সঠিক রূপটি হলো 'With whom did you go to the market?', যেখানে auxiliary verb subject-এর আগে বসে।

questions.question: The complex form of "A rolling stone gathers no moss" is ----
options: Since a stone is rolling, it gathers no moss
Though a stone rolls, it gathers no moss.
A stone what rolls gathers no moss.
A stone that rolls gathers no moss.
questions.explanation:
The complex form uses a relative clause: 'A stone that rolls gathers no moss'.
Complex রূপে relative clause ব্যবহৃত হয়: 'A stone that rolls gathers no moss'।

questions.question: 'India Wins Freedom' is written by ----
questions.explanation:
The book 'India Wins Freedom' was written by Abul Kalam Azad (A. K. Azad).
'India Wins Freedom' গ্রন্থটি আবুল কালাম আজাদ (A. K. Azad) রচনা করেন।

questions.question: Two and two ---- four.
questions.explanation:
When two numbers are added to give a single result, the sum is treated as one idea and takes a singular verb, so 'Two and two makes four.'
দুটি সংখ্যা যোগ করে একক ফল বোঝালে যোগফলকে একবচন ধরা হয় এবং একবচন ক্রিয়া বসে, তাই 'Two and two makes four' সঠিক।

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect (reported) speech of: The mother said to her son, 'May you pass the examination.'
options: The mother wished her son that he might pass the examination
The mother said to her son that he might pass the examination
The mother wished that her son might pass the examination
The mother wished her son that he may pass the examination
questions.explanation:
An optative sentence expressing a wish ('May you...') is reported using 'wished that', and because the reporting verb is past, 'may' changes to 'might'.
ইচ্ছা প্রকাশক (optative) বাক্য 'May you...' পরোক্ষ উক্তিতে 'wished that' দিয়ে লেখা হয় এবং reporting verb past হওয়ায় 'may' পরিবর্তিত হয়ে 'might' হয়।

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Death is more preferable than dishonour
Death is more preferable then dishonour
questions.explanation:
'Preferable' is followed by 'to' (not 'than') and is never used with 'more', so 'Death is preferable to dishonour' is correct.
'Preferable'-এর পরে 'than' নয়, 'to' বসে এবং এর সাথে 'more' ব্যবহার হয় না; তাই 'Death is preferable to dishonour' সঠিক।

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: The jury were unanimous in its opinion
The jury was unanimous in its opinion
The jury was together in its opinion
The jury were unanimous in their opinion
questions.explanation:
When 'jury' acts as one united body it takes a singular verb and the singular pronoun 'its', so 'The jury was unanimous in its opinion' is correct.
'Jury' একক সমষ্টি হিসেবে কাজ করলে একবচন ক্রিয়া ও একবচন সর্বনাম 'its' নেয়, তাই 'The jury was unanimous in its opinion' সঠিক।

questions.question: What is the meaning of the proverb 'Diamond cut diamond'?
options: All that glitters is not gold
Leeches can be identified by looking closely
questions.explanation:
'Diamond cut diamond' means that a clever or strong person is matched by an equally clever or strong one, i.e. the Bengali proverb 'মানিকে মানিক চেনে'.
'Diamond cut diamond' প্রবাদটির অর্থ হলো এক চতুর বা শক্তিশালী ব্যক্তির সাথে সমান চতুর বা শক্তিশালী ব্যক্তির টক্কর, অর্থাৎ 'মানিকে মানিক চেনে'।

questions.question: Who wrote 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty'?
questions.explanation:
The line 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty' comes from John Keats's poem 'Ode on a Grecian Urn'.
'Beauty is truth, truth beauty' পঙক্তিটি জন কিটসের কবিতা 'Ode on a Grecian Urn' থেকে নেওয়া।

questions.question: The number of students seeking admission ----
questions.explanation:
'The number of' + a plural noun takes a singular verb, so 'has increased' is correct.
'The number of' + বহুবচন বিশেষ্যের পরে একবচন ক্রিয়া বসে, তাই 'has increased' সঠিক।

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence ----.
options: Gold and silver is precious metal.
Gold and silver are precious metal.
Gold and silver has precious metal.
Gold and silver have precious metal.
questions.explanation:
'Gold and silver' are two separate substances joined by 'and', so they take the plural verb 'are'.
'Gold and silver' হলো 'and' দ্বারা যুক্ত দুটি ভিন্ন পদার্থ, তাই এদের সাথে বহুবচন ক্রিয়া 'are' বসে।

questions.question: He didn't get ---- job he applied for.
questions.explanation:
The job is a specific one (the one he applied for), so the definite article 'the' is used.
চাকরিটি নির্দিষ্ট (যেটির জন্য সে আবেদন করেছিল), তাই নির্দিষ্ট আর্টিকেল 'the' বসে।

questions.question: Which word is correctly spelt?
questions.explanation:
The correct spelling is 'Adulteration' (a-dul-te-ra-tion), meaning the mixing of impurities.
সঠিক বানান হলো 'Adulteration' (a-dul-te-ra-tion), যার অর্থ ভেজাল মেশানো।

questions.question: He ---- me while I was reading.
questions.explanation:
A short action breaking into an ongoing past action ('was reading') takes the simple past, so 'interrupted' is correct.
অতীতে চলমান কাজের ('was reading') মাঝে ঘটে যাওয়া সংক্ষিপ্ত কাজ simple past হয়, তাই 'interrupted' সঠিক।

questions.question: In 'The sun went down', the underlined word 'down' is used here as a/an:
questions.explanation:
Here 'down' modifies the verb 'went' by showing direction, so it is an adverb.
এখানে 'down' শব্দটি 'went' ক্রিয়াকে বিশেষিত করে দিক নির্দেশ করছে, তাই এটি একটি adverb।

questions.question: Make it interrogative: Nobody believes a liar.
questions.explanation:
A negative assertive sentence starting with 'Nobody' becomes interrogative with 'Who', so it turns into 'Who believes a liar?'
'Nobody' দিয়ে শুরু নেতিবাচক বিবৃতিমূলক বাক্যকে interrogative করতে 'Who' বসে, তাই এটি হয় 'Who believes a liar?'

questions.question: In many ways, riding a bicycle is similar to ----
questions.explanation:
For parallel structure the gerund 'riding' must be compared with another gerund, so 'driving a car' is correct.
সমান্তরাল গঠনের জন্য gerund 'riding'-এর সাথে আরেকটি gerund তুলনা করতে হয়, তাই 'driving a car' সঠিক।

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The girl burst out of tears
The girl burst out with tears
The girl burst out through tears
questions.explanation:
The correct idiom is 'burst into tears', which means to start crying suddenly.
সঠিক বাগধারা হলো 'burst into tears', যার অর্থ হঠাৎ কেঁদে ফেলা।

questions.question: Which of the following is not a form of poetry?
questions.explanation:
Ballad, sonnet and epic are poetic forms, but a 'tale' is a form of narrative prose, not poetry.
Ballad, sonnet ও epic হলো কবিতার রূপ, কিন্তু 'tale' হলো গদ্য আখ্যান, কবিতা নয়।

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correct?
options: He succeeded to win the prize
See the word in the dictionary
questions.explanation:
'He cannot pronounce the word' is correct; the others misuse idiom or preposition (it should be 'succeeded in winning', 'look up the word', and 'at dawn').
'He cannot pronounce the word' সঠিক; বাকিগুলোতে idiom বা preposition ভুল আছে (সঠিক হবে 'succeeded in winning', 'look up the word', 'at dawn')।

questions.question: How many eggs have your hens ---- this month?
questions.explanation:
The transitive verb 'lay' (lay–laid–laid) means to produce eggs, so its past participle 'laid' is used after 'have'.
সকর্মক ক্রিয়া 'lay' (lay–laid–laid) অর্থ ডিম পাড়া, তাই 'have'-এর পরে এর past participle 'laid' বসে।

questions.question: In 'The book that she recommended turned out to be very helpful', the underlined clause 'that she recommended' is a -
questions.explanation:
'That she recommended' comes after a noun and describes it, so it is a relative (adjective) clause.
'That she recommended' অংশটি একটি বিশেষ্যের পরে বসে সেটিকে বিশেষিত করছে, তাই এটি একটি relative (adjective) clause।

questions.question: Public universities are funded by ----.
questions.explanation:
Public universities are financed mainly by the government.
সরকারি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়গুলো মূলত সরকার কর্তৃক অর্থায়িত হয়।

questions.question: What is the passive form of 'Visitors found him playing football.'?
options: Visitors were found playing football by him
He was found playing football by visitors
Visitors found that football was playing by him
He was playing football that was seen by visitors.
questions.explanation:
The object 'him' becomes the subject of the passive voice, giving 'He was found playing football by visitors.'
কর্ম 'him' passive voice-এ কর্তা হয়ে যায়, ফলে বাক্যটি হয় 'He was found playing football by visitors.'

questions.question: Which of the following books is written by Thomas Hardy?
questions.explanation:
'The Return of the Native' is a novel by Thomas Hardy.
'The Return of the Native' হলো টমাস হার্ডির লেখা একটি উপন্যাস।

questions.question: The books ---- to the library are kept in the storage room.
questions.explanation:
The past participle 'given' works like an adjective here (= that were given), so 'given' is correct.
এখানে past participle 'given' বিশেষণের মতো কাজ করছে (= যেগুলো দেওয়া হয়েছিল), তাই 'given' সঠিক।

questions.question: In the sentence 'Still waters run deep', what part of speech is the word 'Still'?
questions.explanation:
'Still' comes before the noun 'waters' and describes it, so it is an adjective.
'Still' শব্দটি 'waters' বিশেষ্যের আগে বসে এটিকে বিশেষিত করছে, তাই এটি একটি adjective।

questions.question: I am not bad ---- tennis.
questions.explanation:
When talking about a skill, 'good/bad' is followed by the preposition 'at', so 'bad at tennis' is correct.
কোনো দক্ষতা বোঝাতে 'good/bad'-এর পরে preposition 'at' বসে, তাই 'bad at tennis' সঠিক।

questions.question: There ---- twelve months in a year.
questions.explanation:
'Twelve months' is plural and states a present, general fact, so the verb is 'are'.
'Twelve months' বহুবচন এবং এটি বর্তমান সর্বজনীন সত্য প্রকাশ করছে, তাই ক্রিয়া 'are' হবে।

questions.question: Which phrase contains words opposed to each other in meaning?
questions.explanation:
'Reproduction' (creating life) and 'death' (end of life) are opposite in meaning.
'Reproduction' (জীবন সৃষ্টি) এবং 'death' (জীবনের সমাপ্তি) অর্থে পরস্পর বিপরীত।

questions.question: Who is the poet of the poem 'Ozymandias'?
questions.explanation:
The sonnet 'Ozymandias' was written by P. B. Shelley.
'Ozymandias' সনেটটি রচনা করেছেন পি. বি. শেলি।

questions.question: The players are ---- tired ---- nervous.
questions.explanation:
The correlative conjunction pair is 'either ... or', so 'either tired or nervous' is correct.
সম্পর্কযুক্ত সংযোজক জোড়াটি হলো 'either ... or', তাই 'either tired or nervous' সঠিক।

questions.question: A person who writes about his own life writes -
questions.explanation:
An account of one's own life written by oneself is called an autobiography.
নিজের জীবন সম্পর্কে নিজে লেখা কাহিনিকে autobiography (আত্মজীবনী) বলা হয়।

questions.question: T. S. Eliot was born in ----.
questions.explanation:
T. S. Eliot was born in St. Louis, Missouri, in the USA, and later became a British citizen.
টি. এস. এলিয়ট যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের সেন্ট লুইস, মিসৌরিতে জন্মগ্রহণ করেন এবং পরে ব্রিটিশ নাগরিক হন।

questions.question: Which of the following is a compound sentence?
options: A drowning man catches at a straw
questions.explanation:
'Do or die' joins two independent clauses with the conjunction 'or', so it is a compound sentence.
'Do or die' বাক্যে 'or' সংযোজক দিয়ে দুটি স্বাধীন clause যুক্ত হয়েছে, তাই এটি একটি compound sentence।

questions.question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'vice versa'?
questions.explanation:
'Vice versa' means that the order or relation of the two things is reversed or exchanged.
'Vice versa' অর্থ দুটি বিষয়ের ক্রম বা সম্পর্ক উল্টে যাওয়া বা পরস্পর বিনিময় হওয়া।

questions.question: What is the verb form of the word 'Bitter'?
questions.explanation:
The verb form of 'bitter' is 'embitter', meaning to make someone feel bitter or resentful.
'Bitter' শব্দের verb রূপ হলো 'embitter', যার অর্থ কাউকে তিক্ত বা বিক্ষুব্ধ করে তোলা।

questions.question: In 'I recognized your voice at once', what type of noun is the underlined word 'voice'?
questions.explanation:
'Voice' names a general kind of thing that many people have, so it is a common noun.
'Voice' একটি সাধারণ শ্রেণির জিনিসের নাম যা অনেকেরই থাকে, তাই এটি common noun।

questions.question: In 'Anybody can apply for the post', the word 'anybody' is a -
questions.explanation:
'Anybody' does not point to any particular person, so it is an indefinite pronoun.
'Anybody' কোনো নির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তিকে নির্দেশ করে না, তাই এটি একটি indefinite pronoun।

questions.question: The idiom 'salt of life' stands for -
questions.explanation:
'Salt of life' figuratively refers to the valuable, worthwhile things that give life meaning and flavour.
'Salt of life' রূপকভাবে জীবনের মূল্যবান ও তাৎপর্যপূর্ণ বিষয়গুলোকে বোঝায়।

questions.question: A 'cardiologist' is a -
questions.explanation:
A cardiologist is a doctor who specialises in the heart, so 'heart specialist' is correct.
Cardiologist হলেন হৃদরোগ বিশেষজ্ঞ চিকিৎসক, তাই 'heart specialist' সঠিক।

questions.question: Did you ---- here before?
questions.explanation:
After the auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb is used, so 'Did you stay here before?' is correct.
সহায়ক ক্রিয়া 'did'-এর পরে ক্রিয়ার base form বসে, তাই 'Did you stay here before?' সঠিক।

questions.question: 'To Daffodils' is a poem written by -
questions.explanation:
The poem 'To Daffodils' was written by Robert Herrick.
'To Daffodils' কবিতাটি রচনা করেছেন রবার্ট হেরিক।

questions.question: The ---- of the camel was found lying by the side of the canal.
questions.explanation:
The dead body of an animal is called a 'carcass', while 'corpse' is used for a dead human body.
মৃত পশুর দেহকে 'carcass' বলা হয়, আর মানুষের মৃতদেহকে বলা হয় 'corpse'।

questions.question: The bird has ---- away.
questions.explanation:
After 'has' the past participle is required, and the past participle of 'fly' is 'flown'.
'has'-এর পরে past participle বসে, এবং 'fly'-এর past participle হলো 'flown'।

questions.question: She went away ----.
questions.explanation:
The present participle 'dancing' describes how she went away, so 'She went away dancing' is correct.
present participle 'dancing' বোঝাচ্ছে সে কীভাবে চলে গেল, তাই 'She went away dancing' সঠিক।

questions.question: Find the correct English translation: 'সকাল থেকে গুঁড়ি গুঁড়ি বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে।'
options: It has been raining from morning.
It has been drizzling since morning.
questions.explanation:
Light, continuous rain from a past point up to now needs 'drizzling' with the present perfect continuous and 'since', giving 'It has been drizzling since morning.'
অতীতের একটি সময় থেকে এ পর্যন্ত চলা গুঁড়ি গুঁড়ি বৃষ্টি বোঝাতে 'drizzling' এবং present perfect continuous ও 'since' লাগে, তাই 'It has been drizzling since morning.' সঠিক।

questions.question: 'A person who held a position before another person' refers to -
questions.explanation:
A person who held an office or position before someone else is that person's predecessor.
যে ব্যক্তি অন্য কারও আগে কোনো পদে ছিলেন, তাকে তার predecessor (পূর্বসূরি) বলা হয়।

questions.question: Each of the boys ---- present in the class.
questions.explanation:
'Each of the' + a plural noun takes a singular verb, so 'is' is correct.
'Each of the' + বহুবচন বিশেষ্যের পরে একবচন ক্রিয়া বসে, তাই 'is' সঠিক।

questions.question: The defeat in the final had an adverse ---- on them.
questions.explanation:
After the article 'an' and the adjective 'adverse', a singular noun is needed, and the noun form is 'effect'.
'an' article ও 'adverse' বিশেষণের পরে একবচন বিশেষ্য দরকার, আর বিশেষ্য রূপটি হলো 'effect'।

questions.question: Nobody knocked him down; it was an ----
questions.explanation:
'Incident' means an event or occurrence, whereas 'accident' stresses an unfortunate, injurious mishap; here it is described as an incident.
'Incident' অর্থ কোনো ঘটনা বা ব্যাপার, আর 'accident' অর্থ দুর্ঘটনা; এখানে বিষয়টিকে একটি incident হিসেবে বর্ণনা করা হয়েছে।

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correct?
options: The good is of inferior quality
The goods is of inferior quality
The goods are of inferior quality
questions.explanation:
'Goods' (meaning merchandise) is always plural and takes a plural verb, so 'The goods are of inferior quality' is correct.
'Goods' (পণ্য অর্থে) সর্বদা বহুবচন এবং বহুবচন ক্রিয়া নেয়, তাই 'The goods are of inferior quality' সঠিক।

questions.question: This could have worked if I ---- been more far-sighted.
questions.explanation:
In a third conditional the 'if'-clause uses the past perfect, so 'if I had been more far-sighted' is correct.
Third conditional-এ 'if'-clause-এ past perfect বসে, তাই 'if I had been more far-sighted' সঠিক।

questions.question: The play 'The Spanish Tragedy' is written by ----
questions.explanation:
'The Spanish Tragedy' was written by the Elizabethan playwright Thomas Kyd.
'The Spanish Tragedy' নাটকটি রচনা করেছেন এলিজাবেথীয় নাট্যকার টমাস কিড।

questions.question: We need two hundred dollars ---- this to pay for everything.
questions.explanation:
'Besides' means 'in addition to', so 'besides this' is correct, whereas 'beside' means 'next to'.
'Besides' অর্থ 'অতিরিক্ত/এছাড়াও', তাই 'besides this' সঠিক; অন্যদিকে 'beside' অর্থ 'পাশে'।

questions.question: In 'Someone sneezed loudly at the back of the hall', the verb 'sneezed' is ----.
questions.explanation:
'Sneezed' takes no object and is followed by an adverb, so it is an intransitive verb.
'Sneezed'-এর কোনো object নেই এবং এর পরে adverb বসেছে, তাই এটি একটি intransitive verb।

questions.question: Though it is raining, ----.
questions.explanation:
'Though/Although' is not paired with 'yet', 'still' or 'but' in the main clause, so 'he will go' is correct.
'Though/Although'-এর সাথে প্রধান clause-এ 'yet', 'still' বা 'but' বসে না, তাই 'he will go' সঠিক।

questions.question: Many a student ---- to qualify the driving test.
questions.explanation:
'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, so 'Many a student fails' is correct.
'Many a'-এর পরে একবচন বিশেষ্য ও একবচন ক্রিয়া বসে, তাই 'Many a student fails' সঠিক।

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correct?
questions.explanation:
'Information' is an uncountable noun taking a singular verb, so 'Your information is false' is correct ('advice' and 'news' are also uncountable).
'Information' একটি অগণনীয় বিশেষ্য যা একবচন ক্রিয়া নেয়, তাই 'Your information is false' সঠিক ('advice' ও 'news'-ও অগণনীয়)।

questions.question: 'Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heaven.' Who wrote this?
questions.explanation:
This famous line is spoken by Satan in John Milton's epic 'Paradise Lost'.
এই বিখ্যাত পঙক্তিটি জন মিল্টনের মহাকাব্য 'Paradise Lost'-এ শয়তানের উক্তি।

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as the national capital, chosen as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest, covering roughly a third of the planet's surface.

questions.question: On which continent is Egypt primarily located?
questions.explanation: Most of Egypt lies in northeastern Africa, though the Sinai Peninsula extends into Asia.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.explanation: Tokyo has served as Japan's capital and seat of government since the 19th century.

questions.question: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which other country?
questions.explanation: Everest straddles the border between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region.

questions.question: The Sahara, the world's largest hot desert, is located on which continent?
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans much of North Africa across more than a dozen countries.

questions.question: In which country is the Great Wall located?
questions.explanation: The Great Wall was built across northern China over many centuries.

questions.question: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean to which other ocean?
questions.explanation: The canal provides a shortcut across the Isthmus of Panama, linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

questions.question: The world's longest international border lies between the United States and which country?
questions.explanation: The U.S.-Canada border is the longest international land border in the world.

questions.question: What is the capital city of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Germany?
questions.explanation: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Italy?
questions.explanation: Rome is the capital of Italy.

questions.question: What is the capital city of China?
questions.explanation: Beijing is the capital of China, while Shanghai is its largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital city of India?
questions.explanation: New Delhi is the capital of India.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt.

questions.question: What is the capital city of South Korea?
questions.explanation: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

questions.question: Which continent contains the greatest number of sovereign countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 sovereign states, more than any other continent.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of Earth's land.

questions.question: Which continent has no permanent human population?
questions.explanation: Antarctica has only temporary research staff and no permanent residents.

questions.question: Which is the only country that occupies an entire continent?
questions.explanation: Australia is the only country that is also a continent.

questions.question: The Isthmus of Panama connects North America to which continent?
questions.explanation: Panama forms the land bridge linking North and South America.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in South America by land area?
questions.explanation: Brazil is by far the largest country in South America.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine flows through Paris.

questions.question: The Mississippi River empties into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi drains into the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.question: How many oceans are recognized in the modern five-ocean model?
questions.explanation: The five recognized oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches along Australia's northeastern coast.

questions.question: Which country shares a land border with only the United States?
questions.explanation: Canada's only land neighbor is the United States, whereas Mexico also borders Guatemala and Belize.

questions.question: The imaginary line at 0° latitude that circles the Earth is called the?
questions.explanation: The Equator is the line of 0° latitude dividing the hemispheres.

questions.question: What is the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is by far the largest tropical rainforest.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation WHO stand for?
questions.explanation: WHO is the World Health Organization, the United Nations' specialized public-health agency.

questions.question: In what year was the United Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The United Nations was established in 1945 after World War II, with its Charter taking effect that October.

questions.question: The League of Nations, the forerunner of the United Nations, was created in the aftermath of which war?
questions.explanation: The League of Nations was founded after World War I to promote collective security.

questions.question: What does the acronym ASEAN stand for?
options: Asian Sovereign Economic Alliance of Nations
Association of Sovereign East Asian Nations
questions.explanation: ASEAN is the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

questions.question: The Commonwealth of Nations is composed largely of former territories of which empire?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth of Nations consists mostly of former parts of the British Empire.

questions.question: The UN agency UNESCO is primarily concerned with which fields?
questions.explanation: UNESCO promotes international cooperation in education, science, and culture.

questions.question: What is the official currency of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian rupee is the official currency of India.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Brazil?
questions.explanation: The real is the official currency of Brazil.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Russia?
questions.explanation: The ruble is the official currency of Russia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of China?
questions.explanation: China's official currency is the yuan, the base unit of the renminbi.

questions.question: A single red maple leaf is the central emblem on the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Canada's flag features a stylized red maple leaf between two red bands.

questions.question: What does the acronym NATO stand for?
questions.explanation: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a collective defense alliance founded in 1949.

questions.question: In which city is the main headquarters of the United Nations located?
questions.explanation: The UN's main headquarters sits on the East River in New York City, though it maintains other major offices worldwide.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of London?
questions.explanation: The River Thames flows through central London before reaching the North Sea.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa, in Ontario, is Canada's capital, not the larger cities of Toronto or Montreal.

questions.question: Which mountain range is traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains in Russia are the conventional dividing line between the European and Asian parts of the landmass.

questions.question: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, shortening the sea route between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Which country is the largest in the world by total area?
questions.explanation: Russia is by far the largest country by area, spanning eleven time zones across Europe and Asia.

questions.question: ASEAN is a regional organization made up of countries from which region?
questions.explanation: ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, unites countries such as Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise capital between rivals Sydney and Melbourne, which are Australia's two largest cities but not the capital.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Ankara replaced Istanbul as the capital in 1923 with the founding of the Turkish Republic, even though Istanbul remains the largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington has been New Zealand's capital since 1865, though Auckland is the larger city.

questions.question: What is the capital of Switzerland?
questions.explanation: Bern is the de facto capital and seat of the federal government, not the larger Zurich or the diplomatic hub Geneva.

questions.question: What has been the capital of Nigeria since 1991?
questions.explanation: The capital was moved from the coastal megacity Lagos to the centrally located, purpose-built city of Abuja in 1991.

questions.question: What is the capital of Laos?
questions.explanation: Vientiane is the capital of Laos; Phnom Penh and Hanoi are the capitals of Cambodia and Vietnam.

questions.question: Which is the northernmost capital city of a sovereign country?
questions.explanation: Reykjavik, Iceland, sits at roughly 64 degrees north, making it the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

questions.question: Which is the highest capital city (seat of government) in the world by elevation?
questions.explanation: La Paz, Bolivia's seat of government, sits at about 3,640 meters, higher than Quito, Bogotá, or Addis Ababa.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Vietnam?
questions.explanation: Vietnam uses the dong; the baht, kip, and riel are the currencies of Thailand, Laos, and Cambodia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Poland?
questions.explanation: Poland uses the złoty and has not adopted the euro; the koruna, forint, and leu belong to Czechia, Hungary, and Romania.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Malaysia uses the ringgit, distinct from Indonesia's rupiah, Thailand's baht, and the Philippine peso.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Hungary?
questions.explanation: Hungary retains the forint and has not joined the eurozone; the złoty, koruna, and leu belong to Poland, Czechia, and Romania.

questions.question: Which currency does Sweden use?
questions.explanation: Sweden uses the krona (spelled with an 'a'), while Denmark and Norway use the krone; Sweden has not adopted the euro.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Iceland?
questions.explanation: Iceland uses its own króna and is not part of the eurozone despite its European location.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Ukraine?
questions.explanation: Ukraine's currency is the hryvnia, introduced in 1996, distinct from the Russian ruble.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Morocco?
questions.explanation: Morocco uses the dirham; dinars are common in other North African states and the riyal is used in Gulf countries.

questions.question: Besides Finnish, what is the other official language of Finland?
questions.explanation: Swedish is co-official with Finnish in Finland, reflecting the country's historical ties to Sweden.

questions.question: What is the national language of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Urdu is Pakistan's national language (with English as an official language), even though Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue.

questions.question: Which country has the only national flag that is not rectangular?
questions.explanation: Nepal's flag is the only non-quadrilateral national flag, formed by two stacked pennant-shaped triangles.

questions.question: Which country's national flag features an AK-47 assault rifle?
questions.explanation: Mozambique's flag uniquely includes an AK-47 with a bayonet, symbolizing defense and vigilance.

questions.question: Which country's national flag prominently depicts a dragon?
questions.explanation: Bhutan's flag features Druk, the Thunder Dragon, reflecting the country's name 'Land of the Thunder Dragon.'

questions.question: Which country's flag depicts the temple of Angkor Wat?
questions.explanation: Cambodia is the only country to feature a building, Angkor Wat, on its national flag.

questions.question: Which country's national flag features a cedar tree in the center?
questions.explanation: Lebanon's flag centers on a green cedar tree, a national symbol referenced even in the Bible.

questions.question: What does the eagle on the Mexican flag's coat of arms depict?
options: An eagle devouring a serpent atop a cactus
questions.explanation: Mexico's flag shows a golden eagle perched on a cactus, devouring a serpent, based on an Aztec founding legend.

questions.question: What emblem appears at the center of Albania's national flag?
questions.explanation: Albania's red flag features a black double-headed eagle, linked to the national hero Skanderbeg.

questions.question: Which sovereign country is entirely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is a landlocked enclave completely encircled by South Africa; Eswatini borders both South Africa and Mozambique.

questions.question: Which two countries share the Caribbean island of Hispaniola?
questions.explanation: Hispaniola is divided between Haiti in the west and the Dominican Republic in the east.

questions.question: The Gambia is almost entirely surrounded by which single country?
questions.explanation: The Gambia is a narrow strip following its river and is enclosed on nearly all sides by Senegal, opening only to the Atlantic.

questions.question: Which is the world's largest landlocked country by area?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan, at about 2.7 million square kilometers, is by far the largest landlocked country in the world.

questions.question: Which two African nations are commonly cited as never having been formally colonized by European powers?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia (despite a brief Italian occupation) and Liberia are traditionally cited as the African states that avoided formal European colonization.

questions.question: Which strait separates Spain from Morocco, linking the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar is the narrow passage between Spain and Morocco connecting the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Mount Everest lies on the border between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The summit of Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet Autonomous Region).

questions.question: In which city are the main institutions of the European Union headquartered, making it the EU's de facto capital?
questions.explanation: Brussels, Belgium, hosts the European Commission and the Council and is considered the EU's de facto capital.

questions.question: Which is the smallest sovereign country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City, an enclave within Rome, is the world's smallest independent state at about 0.44 square kilometers.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from which country?
questions.explanation: The narrow Strait of Gibraltar separates southern Spain in Europe from Morocco in Africa.

questions.question: Which is the deepest freshwater lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the world's deepest lake, reaching over 1,600 meters.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is an enclave entirely encircled by South African territory; Eswatini also borders Mozambique.

questions.question: Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls plunges from a tepui in the Canaima region of Venezuela.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro rises in northeastern Tanzania, near the border with Kenya.

questions.question: How many permanent members sit on the United Nations Security Council?
questions.explanation: There are five permanent members with veto power: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

questions.question: Since 2006, what has served as the administrative capital of Myanmar (Burma)?
questions.explanation: The military government relocated the capital from Yangon to the newly built city of Naypyidaw in 2006.

questions.question: Which city is the constitutional capital of Bolivia?
questions.explanation: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital and home to the judiciary, while La Paz is the seat of the executive and legislature.

questions.question: What is the official administrative capital of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte hosts the national parliament and is the official capital, while Colombo is the commercial hub.

questions.question: Which city is the executive (administrative) capital of South Africa?
questions.explanation: South Africa splits its capital functions: Pretoria is executive, Cape Town legislative, and Bloemfontein judicial.

questions.question: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
questions.explanation: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan; Dushanbe, Tashkent, and Ashgabat are capitals of Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan respectively.

questions.question: What is the capital of Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Thimphu is Bhutan's capital; Kathmandu is Nepal's and Dhaka is Bangladesh's, while Paro is a Bhutanese town known for its airport.

questions.question: What is the capital of Burkina Faso?
questions.explanation: Ouagadougou is Burkina Faso's capital; Bamako, Niamey, and Accra are the capitals of Mali, Niger, and Ghana.

questions.question: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
questions.explanation: Dodoma has been Tanzania's official capital since 1996, though Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and commercial center.

questions.question: What is the official political capital of Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast)?
questions.explanation: Yamoussoukro became the official capital in 1983, while Abidjan remains the economic capital and largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital of Belize?
questions.explanation: Belmopan was built inland and became the capital in 1970 after a hurricane devastated the coastal Belize City.

questions.question: What is the capital of Eritrea?
questions.explanation: Asmara, noted for its modernist architecture, is Eritrea's capital; the others are capitals of Ethiopia, Sudan, and Djibouti.

questions.question: What is the capital of Malawi?
questions.explanation: Lilongwe replaced Zomba as Malawi's capital in 1975; Blantyre remains the commercial center.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkmenistan?
questions.explanation: Ashgabat, famous for its white marble buildings, is Turkmenistan's capital, not Tashkent (Uzbekistan) or Baku (Azerbaijan).

questions.question: What is the capital of Liechtenstein?
questions.explanation: Vaduz is the capital of the microstate Liechtenstein; the others are capitals of Luxembourg, San Marino, and Andorra.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Botswana?
questions.explanation: Botswana's currency is the pula (meaning 'rain'); the rand, kwacha, and birr belong to South Africa, Zambia/Malawi, and Ethiopia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Guatemala?
questions.explanation: Guatemala's currency, the quetzal, is named after its national bird; the others belong to Costa Rica, Honduras, and Nicaragua.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Peru?
questions.explanation: Peru's currency is the sol; the boliviano and real belong to Bolivia and Brazil.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Ghana?
questions.explanation: Ghana uses the cedi; the naira, dalasi, and leone belong to Nigeria, The Gambia, and Sierra Leone.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Costa Rica?
questions.explanation: Costa Rica uses the colón, named after Christopher Columbus (Colón); the others belong to Panama, Guatemala, and Nicaragua.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Paraguay?
questions.explanation: Paraguay's currency is the guaraní, named after its indigenous people and language.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia uses the birr; the nakfa is Eritrea's currency and shillings are used across East African neighbors.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Kazakhstan?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan introduced the tenge in 1993; the som, manat, and ruble belong to Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan/Turkmenistan, and Russia.

questions.question: Which South American country has Dutch as its official language?
questions.explanation: Suriname, a former Dutch colony, is the only South American country where Dutch is the official language; neighboring Guyana uses English.

questions.question: What is the sole official language of Andorra?
questions.explanation: Andorra is the only country in the world with Catalan as its sole official language.

questions.question: Besides German, French, and Italian, what is Switzerland's fourth official language?
questions.explanation: Romansh, spoken by a small minority in the canton of Graubünden, is Switzerland's fourth national and official language.

questions.question: Besides Dutch and French, what is the third official language of Belgium?
questions.explanation: Belgium recognizes German as its third official language, spoken in the country's east; Flemish is simply the local variety of Dutch.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Singapore's four official languages?
questions.explanation: Singapore's four official languages are English, Malay, Mandarin Chinese, and Tamil; Hindi is not among them.

questions.question: Which indigenous language is co-official with Spanish in Paraguay?
questions.explanation: Paraguay is unusual in that Guaraní is co-official with Spanish and widely spoken by the majority of the population.

questions.question: Which is the only country in Central America with English as its official language?
questions.explanation: Belize, a former British colony, is the only Central American nation with English as its official language; its neighbors use Spanish.

questions.question: What is the working (official) language of Ethiopia's federal government?
questions.explanation: Amharic serves as the working language of Ethiopia's federal government, though many other languages are spoken regionally.

questions.question: Besides Switzerland, which country has a square national flag?
questions.explanation: Switzerland and Vatican City are the only sovereign states with square (1:1) national flags.

questions.question: Which country's flag features a copper-colored map of the island itself?
questions.explanation: Cyprus's flag displays a map of the island in copper over two olive branches, symbolizing peace.

cards.back: 60 to 100 beats per minute in a resting adult. Bradycardia is below 60; tachycardia is above 100.
12 to 20 breaths per minute at rest for a healthy adult.
Less than 120 mmHg systolic and less than 80 mmHg diastolic, per current guidelines.
95 to 100 percent as measured by pulse oximetry in a healthy adult.
3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L. Abnormal levels can cause dangerous cardiac arrhythmias.
135 to 145 mEq/L. It is the major cation in the extracellular fluid and regulates fluid balance.
Approximately 70 to 100 mg/dL after at least 8 hours without food.
150,000 to 400,000 per microliter. Platelets are essential for blood clotting.
A drug class that lowers blood pressure by blocking angiotensin-converting enzyme; generic names typically end in -pril (e.g., lisinopril, enalapril).
cards.hint: generic names end in a common suffix

cards.back: Medications that prevent or slow blood clot formation, such as heparin and warfarin; nurses monitor bleeding and clotting labs.
A Latin order meaning nothing by mouth; the patient receives no food or fluids, often before surgery or certain procedures.
A medication order meaning 'as needed,' given when required rather than on a fixed schedule (e.g., PRN pain medication).
An indwelling urinary catheter held in the bladder by an inflated balloon to continuously drain urine into a collection bag.
cards.hint: stays in the bladder to drain urine

cards.front: How many lungs does a person have?
cards.back: Two — a left and a right lung.
N-acetylcysteine (NAC), which replenishes glutathione stores to detoxify the hepatotoxic metabolite NAPQI. Most effective within 8-10 hours of ingestion.
cards.hint: It restores a depleted antioxidant used to neutralize a toxic liver metabolite.

cards.back: Flumazenil, a competitive GABA-A receptor antagonist. Used cautiously because it can precipitate seizures in chronic users or mixed overdoses.
cards.hint: It competitively blocks the same receptor the drug activates.

cards.back: Digoxin immune Fab (Digibind/DigiFab), antibody fragments that bind free digoxin. Indicated for life-threatening dysrhythmias or serum digoxin >10 ng/mL.
cards.hint: It is an antibody fragment that binds the drug directly.

cards.back: Protamine sulfate, a positively charged protein that binds and neutralizes negatively charged heparin. Roughly 1 mg reverses about 100 units of heparin.
cards.hint: A positively charged molecule that binds the negatively charged drug.

cards.back: Vitamin K (phytonadione) for non-urgent reversal; for major bleeding, four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) or fresh frozen plasma for rapid replacement of clotting factors.
cards.hint: The slow agent restores synthesis of the factors the drug suppressed.

cards.back: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L for maintenance. Early toxicity (>1.5) causes tremor, diarrhea, and ataxia; severe toxicity (>2.0) causes seizures and dysrhythmias.
cards.hint: A narrow window under about 1.5 mEq/L.

cards.back: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL. Hypokalemia potentiates toxicity, so potassium must be monitored closely, especially with concurrent diuretics.
cards.hint: Toxicity worsens when a certain electrolyte drops.

cards.front: Therapeutic INR for standard anticoagulation on warfarin
cards.back: 2.0-3.0 for most indications (e.g., atrial fibrillation, DVT/PE). A higher target of 2.5-3.5 is used for mechanical mitral valves.

cards.front: Therapeutic aPTT target for heparin therapy
cards.back: Approximately 1.5-2.5 times the control value (often around 60-80 seconds depending on the lab). Used to monitor unfractionated heparin.
cards.hint: Expressed as a multiple of the control time.

cards.back: A non-allergic reaction from too-rapid vancomycin infusion causing histamine release, producing flushing/erythema of the upper body. Prevented by slowing the infusion.
cards.hint: Related to infusion rate, not a true allergy.

cards.front: Mechanism of ACE inhibitor-induced dry cough
cards.back: ACE inhibitors block breakdown of bradykinin, and bradykinin accumulation in the airways triggers a persistent dry cough. Switching to an ARB usually resolves it.
cards.hint: A vasoactive peptide accumulates because its breakdown is blocked.

cards.front: Key nursing concern with IV potassium administration
cards.back: Never give IV potassium by push/bolus; it must be diluted and infused slowly (generally ≤10 mEq/hr peripherally) with cardiac monitoring, as rapid infusion can cause fatal arrhythmias.
cards.hint: Bolusing this electrolyte can stop the heart.

cards.front: Critical high serum potassium and ECG change
cards.back: A potassium >6.0-6.5 mEq/L is critical; the classic early ECG finding is tall, peaked T waves, progressing to widened QRS and sine-wave patterns leading to arrest.
135-145 mEq/L. Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia risks osmotic demyelination (central pontine myelinolysis), so sodium is corrected slowly.
cards.hint: Correcting it too fast damages the pons.

cards.back: 1.5-2.5 mg/dL (about 0.75-1.25 mmol/L). Hypomagnesemia often accompanies and perpetuates refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia.
cards.hint: Low levels make it hard to correct two other electrolytes.

cards.back: IV calcium gluconate. It antagonizes the neuromuscular and cardiac effects seen with hypermagnesemia (e.g., loss of deep tendon reflexes, respiratory depression).
cards.hint: A divalent cation that physiologically opposes the toxic electrolyte.

cards.back: Atropine (blocks muscarinic effects) plus pralidoxime (2-PAM, which reactivates acetylcholinesterase). Atropine dries secretions; pralidoxime restores the enzyme.
cards.hint: Two drugs: one dries secretions, one regenerates the inhibited enzyme.

cards.back: Glucagon, which increases intracellular cAMP independently of beta-receptors, improving heart rate and contractility. Calcium and high-dose insulin/glucose are adjuncts.
cards.hint: A pancreatic hormone that raises cAMP bypassing the blocked receptor.

cards.back: Hydroxocobalamin (binds cyanide to form cyanocobalamin), or the cyanide antidote kit (sodium nitrite plus sodium thiosulfate).
cards.hint: One option is a form of vitamin B12.

cards.back: Deferoxamine, a chelating agent that binds free iron to form ferrioxamine, which is excreted renally (may turn urine reddish/'vin rose').
cards.hint: A chelator whose complex may tint the urine reddish.

cards.front: Antidote for methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning
cards.back: Fomepizole (preferred) or ethanol, which inhibit alcohol dehydrogenase and prevent formation of toxic metabolites. Hemodialysis removes the toxin in severe cases.
cards.hint: It blocks the enzyme that converts the alcohol into toxic acids.

cards.front: Vancomycin trough goal for serious infections
cards.back: A trough of 15-20 mcg/mL (or AUC-guided dosing) for serious MRSA infections. Elevated troughs increase nephrotoxicity risk.
cards.hint: The pre-dose level for deep/serious infections, in the high teens.

cards.back: Neuromuscular abnormalities (clonus, hyperreflexia, rigidity), autonomic instability (hyperthermia, tachycardia), and altered mental status. Often from combining serotonergic drugs.
cards.hint: Think excess of one neurotransmitter: muscles, autonomics, and mind.

cards.front: Zero-order kinetics drug example and significance
cards.back: Phenytoin and ethanol follow zero-order kinetics: a constant amount is metabolized per unit time regardless of concentration, so small dose increases can cause disproportionate toxicity.
cards.hint: A fixed quantity, not a fixed fraction, is cleared per hour.

cards.front: Normal total serum calcium and corrected calcium concept
cards.back: 8.5-10.5 mg/dL total. Because roughly half is albumin-bound, low albumin falsely lowers total calcium, so a corrected calcium (or ionized calcium) should be assessed.
cards.hint: A protein it binds to affects the reported value.

cards.front: Calculating and interpreting the anion gap
cards.back: Anion gap = Na - (Cl + HCO3); normal is about 8-12 mEq/L. A high anion gap metabolic acidosis suggests causes such as ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, or toxic ingestions.
cards.hint: Subtract the two main anions from sodium.

cards.back: Hypertension (widening pulse pressure), bradycardia, and irregular respirations indicate rising intracranial pressure and impending brain herniation, a neurosurgical emergency.
cards.hint: A late, ominous sign of pressure inside the skull.

cards.back: SIADH: excess ADH causes water retention, dilutional hyponatremia, and concentrated urine. Diabetes insipidus: ADH deficiency/resistance causes dilute polyuria, dehydration, and hypernatremia.
cards.hint: Too much versus too little of the water-conserving hormone.

cards.back: Acute cortisol deficiency causing hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, and shock. Treatment is immediate IV hydrocortisone plus fluid and electrolyte resuscitation.
cards.hint: Life-threatening lack of the stress hormone; give steroids fast.

cards.back: A life-threatening hyperthyroid emergency with high fever, severe tachycardia/arrhythmias, agitation, and delirium. Managed with beta-blockers, thionamides, iodine, and cooling.
cards.hint: Extreme overactivity of the thyroid; think fever and racing heart.

cards.front: Largest planet in the Solar System?
cards.back: Jupiter — its mass is more than twice that of all the other planets combined.

cards.front: Which gas do plants absorb to make food?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide — plants use it during photosynthesis to produce glucose and release oxygen.
Canberra — it was purpose-built as the capital, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
The cheetah — it can reach about 112 km/h (70 mph) in short bursts.

cards.front: How many bones are in the adult human body?
cards.back: 206 — babies are born with around 300, many of which fuse together as they grow.
William Shakespeare — the English playwright wrote the tragedy around 1595.
Diamond — a crystalline form of carbon, it scores a perfect 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
Au — derived from the Latin word 'aurum', meaning shining dawn.

cards.front: First person to walk on the Moon?
cards.back: Neil Armstrong — he stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission.
Vatican City — only about 0.44 square kilometers, entirely surrounded by Rome, Italy.

cards.front: Speed of light in a vacuum?
cards.back: About 299,792 kilometers per second — roughly 300,000 km/s, the universe's speed limit.
The Pacific Ocean — it covers about a third of the planet's surface, more than all land combined.

cards.front: How many hearts does an octopus have?
cards.back: Three — two pump blood to the gills and one circulates it to the rest of the body.

cards.front: How many days are in a week?
cards.back: Seven.

cards.front: What is H₂O commonly known as?
cards.back: Water.
You cannot simultaneously know a particle's exact position and momentum; the more precisely one is measured, the less precisely the other can be known.
cards.hint: A foundational limit in quantum mechanics involving pairs of properties.

cards.back: Within a flowing fluid, an increase in the fluid's speed corresponds to a decrease in its pressure.
cards.hint: Helps explain lift over an aircraft wing.

cards.back: The lowest possible temperature, 0 kelvin (-273.15 C), at which particle thermal motion is minimized.
cards.hint: The bottom of the Kelvin scale.

cards.back: The emission of electrons from a material when light of sufficient frequency strikes it; Einstein's explanation earned him the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.
cards.hint: Evidence that light behaves as discrete packets of energy.

cards.back: A state in which certain materials conduct electricity with exactly zero resistance below a critical temperature.
cards.hint: Enables persistent currents and magnetic levitation.

cards.back: The change in observed frequency of a wave when the source and observer move relative to each other.
cards.hint: Why a passing siren's pitch drops.

cards.back: The number of particles in one mole of a substance, approximately 6.022 x 10^23.
cards.hint: Links the macroscopic mole to the count of atoms or molecules.

cards.back: Different structural forms of the same element, such as diamond, graphite, graphene, and fullerenes for carbon.
Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
cards.hint: They share a place on the periodic table but differ in mass.

cards.front: Most abundant element in the universe
cards.back: Hydrogen, which makes up roughly three-quarters of the universe's normal (baryonic) matter by mass.
A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction by lowering its activation energy without being consumed.
cards.hint: Speeds a reaction but is regenerated at the end.

cards.back: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine through hydrogen bonds.
cards.hint: Four letters that pair in fixed couples.

cards.back: The cellular structure that assembles proteins by translating messenger RNA into chains of amino acids.
The maintenance of a stable internal environment by an organism despite external changes.
cards.hint: Keeping conditions like temperature and pH balanced.

cards.back: Mitosis produces two identical diploid cells for growth and repair, while meiosis produces four genetically varied haploid gametes for reproduction.
cards.hint: One makes body cells, the other makes sex cells.

cards.back: The maximum mass (about 1.4 solar masses) a stable white dwarf can have before collapsing into a neutron star or supernova.
cards.hint: A mass threshold for a certain kind of stellar remnant.

cards.back: The blue glow emitted when a charged particle travels faster than the speed of light in a medium such as water.
cards.hint: Often seen in the water of nuclear reactor cores.

cards.back: Fluorine, which has the strongest tendency of any element to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond.
cards.hint: A small, highly reactive halogen at the top right of the table.

cards.back: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to counteract the change and re-establish equilibrium.
cards.hint: About how equilibria respond to stress like pressure or concentration.

cards.back: Uranium (atomic number 92) is generally considered the heaviest element that occurs naturally in significant amounts.
cards.hint: A radioactive metal used as nuclear fuel.

cards.back: Also called the citric acid cycle, a series of reactions in the mitochondria that oxidize acetyl-CoA to produce energy carriers like NADH and FADH2.
cards.hint: A central hub of cellular respiration.

cards.back: Programmed cell death, a controlled process the body uses to eliminate damaged or unneeded cells.
cards.hint: Cellular self-destruction that is orderly, not accidental.

cards.back: The idea that mitochondria and chloroplasts originated as free-living bacteria engulfed by early eukaryotic cells.
cards.hint: Explains why certain organelles have their own DNA.

cards.back: A rapid diversification of complex animal life about 540 million years ago, when most major animal phyla first appear in the fossil record.
cards.hint: A burst of biodiversity early in the Paleozoic.

cards.back: The treaties that ended the Thirty Years' War and helped establish the modern principle of state sovereignty.
cards.hint: A 17th-century settlement often tied to the idea of the nation-state.

cards.back: One of the earliest and most complete written legal codes, issued by the Babylonian king Hammurabi around 1754 BCE.
cards.hint: An ancient Mesopotamian law code famous for retributive justice.

cards.back: The 1814-1815 conference that redrew Europe's map and sought a balance of power after Napoleon's defeat.
The 1868 political revolution that restored imperial rule in Japan and launched rapid modernization and industrialization.
The meeting where European powers set rules for the colonial partition of Africa, largely ignoring African peoples.
Antarctica, a cold desert of about 14 million square kilometers, is the world's largest desert by area.
cards.hint: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat.

cards.back: Present, appearing, or found everywhere at the same time. Example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.
Lasting for a very short time; fleeting. Example: The beauty of the cherry blossoms is ephemeral, gone within days.
Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Example: She kept meticulous records of every expense.
Truthful and straightforward; frank and honest in speech. Example: He gave a candid assessment of the team's weaknesses.
To force yourself to do something unpleasant or difficult that you have been avoiding. Example: I finally bit the bullet and booked the dentist appointment.
To do or say something to relieve tension and start conversation in a social situation. Example: He told a joke to break the ice at the meeting.
Something that is very easy to do. Example: The exam was a piece of cake for her.
Feeling slightly ill or unwell. Example: I'm staying home today because I'm feeling under the weather.
Use 'fewer' for countable nouns and 'less' for uncountable nouns. Example: Fewer cars means less traffic.
'Its' is the possessive form (belonging to it); 'it's' is a contraction of 'it is' or 'it has'. Example: It's raining, and the dog wagged its tail.
'Who' is the subject of a verb; 'whom' is the object of a verb or preposition. Example: Who called? / To whom did you speak?
Formed with 'have/has' + past participle; it links a past action to the present. Example: I have finished my homework.
Cats — most nouns add "-s".
Cold.
Walked — regular verbs add "-ed".
Having a keen mental insight or sharp discernment; quick to notice and understand things.
cards.hint: Think of someone who sees through a situation instantly.

cards.back: To deliberately make something obscure, unclear, or confusing, often to mislead.
Optimistic or cheerfully confident, especially in a difficult or uncertain situation.
cards.hint: Originally linked to blood and a hopeful temperament.

cards.back: Carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection; done merely as a routine duty.
(Of a voice or words) sweet, smooth, and pleasant to hear, as if flowing like honey.
cards.hint: Its Latin root refers to honey.

cards.back: Lasting for a very short time; transitory.
cards.hint: A mayfly lives only a day.

cards.back: A person who flatters powerful people excessively in order to gain advantage; a servile flatterer.
Reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little by nature.
cards.hint: The quiet type who rarely speaks up.

cards.back: Very attentive to detail and accuracy; hard to please and concerned about cleanliness or precision.
Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way but with harmful effects.
cards.hint: A disease that spreads quietly before symptoms appear.

cards.back: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.
A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
Present, appearing, or found everywhere at once.
Bewildered, puzzled, or lost in thought. It does NOT mean amused, despite the similar spelling.
To avoid getting to the main point; to speak evasively instead of addressing the issue directly.
cards.hint: Circling a topic instead of tackling it head-on.

cards.back: Showing a lack of courage or determination; timid and cowardly.
cards.hint: A very unflattering word for a coward.

cards.back: Too great, extreme, or sacred to be expressed in words.
cards.hint: Related to being unable to speak of something.

cards.back: Eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant and hostile.
Looking or sounding sad, mournful, and dismal, often exaggeratedly so.
cards.hint: Think of a gloomy, drawn-out sigh.

cards.back: Stubbornly resistant to authority, discipline, or control; obstinately uncooperative.
cards.hint: A mule that refuses to move.

cards.back: To use ambiguous or evasive language in order to conceal the truth or avoid committing oneself.
Just begun and so not fully formed or developed; rudimentary.
Bitter, harsh, and abusive in language; full of scathing criticism.
cards.hint: A verbal attack full of venom.

cards.back: Using very few words; terse or concise to the point of seeming blunt.
Extremely idealistic, unrealistic, and impractical, in pursuit of lofty but unattainable goals.
cards.hint: Named after a knight who tilted at windmills.

cards.back: Stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so; apparent rather than actual.
cards.hint: The reason given on the surface, possibly not the real one.

cards.back: To weaken, drain of energy, or exhaust. It does NOT mean to energize despite the deceptive spelling.
cards.hint: The prefix looks like 'energy' but the meaning is the opposite.

cards.back: Traditionally means excessive, cloying, and insincere (e.g., 'fulsome praise'), not simply abundant or generous.
cards.hint: Compliments so lavish they feel fake.

cards.back: To speak or act evasively in order to avoid telling the truth; to be deliberately misleading.
cards.hint: Dodging a straight answer, close in sense to equivocate.

cards.back: Extremely old, outdated, or antiquated; literally 'before the biblical flood.'
Canberra, a purpose-built city chosen as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne.
Russia, covering about 17.1 million km² across Europe and Asia — nearly twice the size of second-place Canada.
Ottawa, located in the province of Ontario on the Ottawa River.
India, which overtook China in 2023 and now has over 1.4 billion people.
Brasília, a planned city inaugurated in 1960 to replace Rio de Janeiro as the capital.
The Sahara in North Africa, spanning roughly 9.2 million km². (Antarctica is the largest desert overall, as a cold desert.)
Ankara, which replaced Istanbul as capital in 1923 under Atatürk.
Vatican City, an independent city-state of about 0.44 km² enclosed within the city of Rome.
Pretoria. South Africa uniquely has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial).
Astana, which was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 but reverted to Astana in 2022.
The Pacific Ocean, covering roughly one-third of Earth's surface — larger than all land combined.
Wellington, situated at the southern tip of the North Island and the world's southernmost national capital.
Paris.
Asia.
The Pacific Ocean.
Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial).
Abuja, a planned central city that replaced Lagos as capital in 1991.
Bern is the seat of government ('federal city'); Switzerland has no formal constitutional capital.
La Paz, Bolivia, sits at roughly 3,640 m (about 11,900 ft) in the Andes.

cards.front: Northernmost capital of a sovereign state
cards.back: Reykjavik, Iceland.

cards.front: Southernmost capital of a sovereign state
cards.back: Wellington, New Zealand.
China and Russia each share land borders with 14 countries, the most of any nation.

cards.front: Country completely surrounded by South Africa
cards.back: Lesotho, a mountainous kingdom that is an enclave entirely within South Africa.
The Canada-United States border, about 8,891 km (5,525 mi) including the Alaska stretch.
Canada, with roughly 202,000 km of coastline owing to its many Arctic islands.
The military control line dividing Indian- and Pakistani-administered Kashmir.
The approximate line dividing North and South Korea; the DMZ roughly follows it.
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Jakarta, Indonesia; ASEAN groups Southeast Asian states (10 members, with Timor-Leste admitted as the 11th in 2025).
32 members; Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in March 2024.
Astana. It was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 but reverted to Astana in 2022.
cards.hint: Reverted from a former president's name.

cards.back: Naypyidaw, a planned city that replaced Yangon (Rangoon) as capital around 2005-2006.
cards.hint: A planned inland city; not Yangon.

cards.back: Sucre is the constitutional capital; La Paz is the seat of government (executive and legislature).
Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, a suburb of Colombo; Colombo remains the commercial hub.
cards.hint: A long-named suburb of the largest city.

cards.back: Yamoussoukro is the official political capital; Abidjan is the economic capital and largest city.
Dodoma is the official capital; Dar es Salaam is the largest city and former capital.
Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan, each landlocked and surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries.
cards.hint: One in the Alps, one in Central Asia.

cards.back: The disputed border between Afghanistan and Pakistan, drawn in 1893.
The 1947 boundary that divided British India into the new states of India and Pakistan.
The disputed boundary between India's Arunachal Pradesh and China/Tibet, drawn in 1914.
The post-World War II border between Germany and Poland, following two rivers.
cards.hint: Two rivers give it its name.

cards.back: Vienna, Austria, even though no OPEC member is European.
An intelligence-sharing alliance of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
Geneva, Switzerland.
cards.hint: A Swiss diplomatic hub, not the capital.

cards.back: Lyon, France.
